prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: ফসল মৌসুমভিত্তিক বপন, কর্তন ও ফলন সূচি (language bn).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "ফসল" · longest unbreakable word 69px · one-line width 149px
  col 2: header "বপন" · longest unbreakable word 66px · one-line width 263px
  col 3: header "কাটা" · longest unbreakable word 68px · one-line width 239px
  col 4: header "ফলন (টন/হেক্টর)" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 108px
  col 5: header "মন্তব্য" · longest unbreakable word 68px · one-line width 1035px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r1B: widths [90, 87, 89, 63, 111] · table 441×1859px · row heights [83, 339, 269, 315, 292, 269, 292] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 14 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 81px
Design r1C: widths [90, 88, 90, 63, 140] · table 472×1417px · row heights [83, 269, 199, 222, 199, 199, 246] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 11 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 112px
Design r2A: widths [90, 87, 89, 63, 195] · table 525×999px · row heights [83, 176, 129, 153, 153, 153, 153] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 165px
Design r2B: widths [90, 87, 89, 63, 250] · table 580×836px · row heights [83, 153, 106, 129, 129, 106, 129] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 220px
Design r2C: widths [90, 115, 110, 63, 185] · table 564×1069px · row heights [83, 176, 153, 176, 153, 153, 176] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 204px
Design r3A: widths [90, 93, 93, 83, 300] · table 660×720px · row heights [83, 106, 106, 106, 106, 106, 106] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 300px
Design r3B: widths [96, 112, 106, 88, 340] · table 743×650px · row heights [60, 106, 106, 83, 106, 83, 106] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 383px
Design r3C: widths [118, 94, 94, 82, 260] · table 649×766px · row heights [83, 129, 106, 129, 106, 106, 106] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 289px

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}

log.raw: {"preferred":["r3A"],"acceptable":["r3B","r3C","r2B","r2A"],"bad":[{"design":"r1B","why":"The comment column collapses to 111px, producing 14-line comment cells and a 1859px-tall table; yield ranges also split across lines."},{"design":"r1C","why":"The comment column is still only 140px, leaving 11-line cells and a 1417px table; yield ranges split, so the narrow-table compromise fails."},{"design":"r2C","why":"Width is misallocated: already-adequate date columns get 115/110px while the long comment column gets only 185px, yielding 7-line comments, a 1069px table, and split yield ranges."}],"contrast":null,"ranges":[[90,104],[87,106],[89,106],[80,94],[285,340]],"rationale":"r3A is the best balance: the comment column gets 300px, enough to hold the longest comment in four lines, while the table stays at 660px rather than 743px. Its 83px yield column keeps ranges such as ৫.৮–৬.৪ on one line, and 90/93/93px keep every Bengali word intact. Horizontal scrolling is unavoidable given a 1035px one-line comment width, so I accept it rather than collapsing comments into 11–14-line strips.","principles":{"general":["Give the column with the longest prose the largest share; equal or symmetric widths waste space on short identifiers and force tall comment cells.","Numbers, ranges and identifiers should not wrap at dashes or within units; set a minimum width from the longest atomic value, not just the longest word.","When a table cannot fit, choose a deliberate scroll width and preserve scan rhythm; a slightly wider table can be better than a very tall one."],"specific":["This table's comment column has a 1035px one-line width, so it dominates; the other four columns are short schedule and yield fields.","The yield column needs about 80px to keep ranges on one line, even though its longest word is only 42px.","Column 1 cannot go below 90px without splitting its 69px longest word; extra width there yields little because its labels still wrap to two lines."]},"tradeoffs":"A narrower 525–580px table reduces horizontal scrolling but forces 6–7-line comments and splits yield ranges; a 660px table is easier to read but requires nearly two screen widths. r3B's extra 83px improves the date columns but does not reduce the tallest comment below four lines.","uncertain":"Whether the phone reader prefers less horizontal scroll (r2B/r2A) or more readable comments (r3A) depends on context; the exact 4-to-5-line threshold for the comment column is approximate."}
